articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches a whopping 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously-named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Chrome also fixed its fourth zero-day this year because apparently browsers are just vulnerability slot machines now.

articles.title: Bug of the year (so far)? Nasty cPanel vulnerability probably exploited as a 0-day
articles.summary: Critical cPanel authentication bypass vulnerability exploited in the wild since February, giving attackers root access to millions of domains. Emergency patches are out, but the horse has already left the barn and burned down the internet.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence hackers exploited old router flaws to mass-harvest Microsoft Office authentication tokens. Classic move: why break into the front door when you can own the entire neighborhood through forgotten IoT garbage?

articles.title: Cyber proxy wars escalate as hackers shift to infrastructure targets
articles.summary: Sri Lanka loses over $3 million in two separate cyber incidents while recovering from economic crisis. Nothing says 'we're getting back on our feet' like having hackers empty your digital piggy bank twice in a row.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: Public records laws exposed ALPR surveillance abuse, so naturally states want to block transparency by changing the laws. Can't have citizens knowing how badly their license plates are being stalked, that would be inconvenient.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new VPN-targeting law goes into effect, predictably driving surge in VPN usage as residents scramble for privacy. It's almost like authoritarian overreach creates the very behavior it tries to prevent.

articles.title: Democratic Leaders Wanted to Control the Maine Senate Race. Their Pick Just Dropped Out.
articles.summary: Ron Wyden pisses off NSA bootlickers by questioning secret surveillance, Tom Cotton threatens 'consequences.' Wyden continues his legendary streak of being the only senator who actually read the Constitution.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider senior member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft from 2022 SMS phishing campaigns. Another one bites the dust in the eternal game of cat and mouse.

articles.title: Utah’s New Law Targeting VPNs Goes Into Effect Next Week
articles.summary: Germany doxes 'UNKN,' the elusive Russian mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware gangs responsible for 130+ cyber sabotage acts. Daniil Shchukin's anonymity finally cracked—turns out even ghost kings cast shadows.

articles.title: Poisoned Ruby Gems and Go Modules Exploit CI Pipelines for Credential Theft
articles.summary: Two cybersecurity professionals get 4-year sentences for facilitating BlackCat ransomware attacks in 2023. The ultimate insider threat: when the people paid to protect you decide crime pays better.
